rule: This register is the stratum's own non-claims, recorded per surface as `hardened` (a change landed), `measured` (a passing court covers the surface) or `not-claimed` (explicitly outside this stratum). It is authored, not derived: the `HOSTILE-BOUNDARY-REGISTER` court in forensics/tools/phase18_courts.py re-reads the live courts registry and fails the stratum if any recorded classification, capacity, count or evidence value here has drifted from what the courts actually show (docs/PHASE-18-SUBPHASES.md section 3.5). A surface the corpus does not reach is `measured` (covered but only bounded) or `not-claimed`, never `hardened`.

surfaces.surface: the TLS record layer (the SSL_accept / SSL_connect record reader)
surfaces.finding: the malformed-record corpus is driven through the record reader with crash/OOM/timeout detection and an authority-linked differential control
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened: no change to the record layer landed in this stratum; the court says the corpus it drove produced the recorded dispositions, not that the parser is safe (sections 3.1 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the handshake-message reader (ClientHello / ServerHello flights)
surfaces.finding: malformed handshake headers and truncated/oversized bodies are driven on both sides
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened; the corpus is a fixed enumeration rather than a fuzzer, and it is not a coverage claim (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: TLS extension bodies (key_share, supported_versions, ALPN, SNI, signature_algorithms)
surfaces.finding: malformed extension bodies are driven on both sides
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened; the extension parser is exercised, not proven (section 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the X.509 DER containers: d2i_X509, d2i_X509_CRL, d2i_X509_REQ
surfaces.finding: truncated, oversized and ill-formed DER containers are driven on both sides
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened: no X.509 reader changed in this stratum; a bounded differential result over the corpus (sections 3.1 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: X.509 extension bodies (d2i_X509_EXTENSION, d2i_X509_EXTENSIONS, X509V3_EXT_d2i)
surfaces.finding: duplicate / unknown / critical extensions and malformed name constraints and SAN are driven
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: the ASN.1 value readers (d2i_ASN1_TYPE, d2i_GENERAL_NAMES, d2i_ASN1_GENERALIZEDTIME, d2i_ASN1_UTCTIME, d2i_X509_ALGOR, d2i_X509_PUBKEY)
surfaces.finding: ASN.1 length bombs, deep nesting, indefinite-length misuse, time/bit-string edges and bad signature AlgorithmIdentifiers are driven
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened; the readers are exercised, not proven memory-safe (sections 3.1 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: the PEM containers (PEM_read_bio_X509, PEM_read_bio_X509_CRL, PEM_read_bio_X509_REQ)
surfaces.finding: bad base64, missing / extra delimiters and wrong labels are driven through the PEM readers
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: the BN primitive paths: BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime and BN_mod_inverse over a 255-bit prime
surfaces.finding: both BN paths measure `separated` -- the two BN separations are recorded as findings, not failed
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened: the reduced engine's BN square-and-multiply core carries this implementation's timing profile by its own module documentation (src/bn/exp.rs); the court's contract is to record the separation with a sensitivity-proven instrument, not to claim constant time (section 3.6).

surfaces.surface: RSA_private_decrypt (C RT exponents of two 1024-bit keys)
surfaces.finding: independent at the 50 percent floor
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened; the screen's resolution is the 50 percent floor (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: EC_POINT_mul on P-256 (the constant-time ladder)
surfaces.finding: independent at the 50 percent floor
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: CRYPTO_memcmp over a 4 KiB tag (the primitive AES-GCM's finish and the Poly1305 check are built on)
surfaces.finding: independent at the 50 percent floor; the sensitivity control varies it and is caught
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened (sections 3.1 and 3.2).

surfaces.surface: EVP_KDF HKDF extract+expand (the TLS 1.3 key schedule's core)
surfaces.finding: independent at the 50 percent floor
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: secret dependence below the 50 percent floor
surfaces.finding: outside the screen's resolution
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a secret dependence below the 50 percent floor is reported `independent` and is outside this screen's resolution, so no constant-time behaviour below the floor is claimed (sections 3.1 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH (16384) record write / record-encryption inner buffer -- the previous greater-than-16-KiB overflow's concrete case
surfaces.finding: the write path fragments at SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH; N = 16383/16384/16385/32768/65536 round-trip on both sides
surfaces.note: hardened: a change landed (the earlier greater-than-16-KiB write overflow is fixed, not merely bounded) and the court drives it at, below and above 16384 (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the tls13_encrypt_record inner [u8; TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN+1] contract
surfaces.finding: recorded as merely unsafe to use directly, not fixed
surfaces.note: measured, not hardened: tls13_encrypt_record copies `len` bytes into its inner buffer without checking `len`; the fragmenting caller bounds it, but the function's own # Safety contract does not, so it is recorded rather than silently fixed (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the handshake-message reassembly buffer Ssl::rd_msg_buf / TLS13_HS_BUF_LEN (16384)
surfaces.finding: the read path is measured at, below and above its capacity and rejects above it
surfaces.note: measured, not fixed: read-hs-below/at are parsed and rejected as malformed and read-hs-above is rejected; every disposition is an error, none a crash (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the record-body store Ssl::rec_body (17000)
surfaces.finding: the record-body store's own bound is measured at, below and above 17000
surfaces.note: measured, not fixed: read-body-at (17000) reads the whole body then rejects on the 16384-byte handshake cap; read-body-above (17001) is refused before the body; the candidate consumes 17005/5 bytes where the authority stops at 5 -- recorded, not fixed (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the injected-failure control ctrl-rlimit (RLIMIT_DATA exhaustion)
surfaces.finding: the allocation failure is driven and observed
surfaces.note: measured: the control lowers RLIMIT_DATA to the child's VmData + 8 MiB and requests a 256 MiB allocation, which must fail and raise the engine's own ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the injected ASN.1 reader allocation control ctrl-d2i
surfaces.finding: d2i_X509 returns NULL over a DER that declares a 64 MiB content under the bound
surfaces.note: measured: the ASN.1 reader's own allocation is driven rather than assumed (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the injected wrapper-allocator control ctrl-hook (CRYPTO_set_mem_functions)
surfaces.finding: the wrapper allocator is observed with no abort or UB
surfaces.note: measured: a wrapper allocator that fails a chosen CRYPTO allocation is installed through CRYPTO_set_mem_functions; the candidate records a divergence from the authority's install result, not a crash (section 3.4).

surfaces.surface: the DER/PEM writers and serialisers (i2d_X509*, PEM_write_*)
surfaces.finding: no court drives an encoder
surfaces.note: not-claimed: this stratum's corpora are malformed *inputs*; no i2d_*/PEM_write_* path is driven, so none is claimed.

surfaces.surface: certificate chain / policy verification (X509_verify_cert, name constraints enforcement)
surfaces.finding: no court drives verification
surfaces.note: not-claimed: RT-HOSTILE-X509 drives the DER/PEM *readers* and extension *parsers*, not the chain/policy verifier (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: the full TLS 1.3 state machine (resumption, key updates, post-handshake auth)
surfaces.finding: no court drives the full state machine
surfaces.note: not-claimed: RT-HOSTILE-TLS drives the record/flight readers with malformed bytes, not a complete multi-flight session (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: coverage-guided fuzzing
surfaces.finding: the corpora are fixed enumerations
surfaces.note: not-claimed: the hostile corpora are fixed enumerations re-derived by their generators and re-verified byte for byte, not a fuzzer; a surface no entry reaches is not counted as passing (section 3.1).

surfaces.surface: a constant-time / secret-independence proof
surfaces.finding: the CT court is a bounded screen
surfaces.note: not-claimed: CT-PRIMITIVES is a bounded work-independence screen at a stated resolution with a proven-sensitive control, not a proof of constant-time behaviour, not a wall-clock claim and not an attack claim (sections 3.1, 3.2 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: a wall-clock timing-attack claim
surfaces.finding: no attack is demonstrated
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a `separated` BN path is a recorded finding about this implementation's timing profile, not a demonstrated attack (section 3.6).

surfaces.surface: a memory-safety proof
surfaces.finding: the memory court is a bounded measurement
surfaces.note: not-claimed: RT-MEM-HARDENING drives the recorded capacities at, below and above the bound; it is a bounded measurement, not a memory-safety proof (sections 3.4 and 3.6).

surfaces.surface: library parity for any symbol
surfaces.finding: no parity is claimed
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a passing hostile court is a bounded differential or property result over the corpus it drives; PARITY_VERIFIED is not claimed for any symbol by this stratum (section 3.6).

surfaces.surface: a security proof
surfaces.finding: the register records a boundary, not a guarantee
surfaces.note: not-claimed: a passing hostile court is a bounded result over the corpus it drove, and a register entry is a record of a boundary, not a guarantee that the boundary cannot be crossed (docs/PHASE-18-SUBPHASES.md section 0).
